new_packages.label: הַדַּעַת וְהַשִּׁדּוּךְ
new_packages.reason: The Torah's central and most explicit bechina cluster is around da'at. Da'at is explicitly called the mediator between two opposites (הַמְתַוֵּךְ בֵּין שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים). Da'at-in-actuality (yotze mipihu = going forth from the mouth) is called a bechina of 'מִפִּיו דַּעַת וּתְבוּנָה'. The tzaddik saying Torah is called a bechina of a matchmaker (מְשַׁדֵּךְ שִׁדּוּכִין). And the word שִׁידּוּךְ is an acronym for 'שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת וְתוֹרָה' — making shidduch a bechina of the priestly/tzaddik function of guarding da'at and Torah. These three or more concepts — da'at, shidduch, bar da'at as matchmaker — form an independent domain connected by explicit bechina language that is entirely absent from the current dataset.

proposed_nodes.role: the act of matching two opposites, bechina of da'at's function
the tzaddik as embodiment of da'at-in-action
da'at in potential — cannot yet bridge the opposites
da'at in actuality — exits through the tzaddik's Torah, enabling the shidduch

source_quotes: הַדַּעַת מְשַׁדֵּךְ כָּל הַשִּׁדּוּכִים, כִּי כָּל הַשִּׁדּוּכִים הֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים, וְהַדַּעַת הוּא הַמְתַוֵּךְ בֵּין שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים
יוֹצֵא הַדַּעַת בִּבְחִינַת: מִפִּיו דַּעַת וּתְבוּנָה
כְּשֶׁהַצַּדִּיק אוֹמֵר תּוֹרָה הוּא בְּחִינַת מְשַׁדֵּךְ שִׁדּוּכִין
וְזֶה אוֹתִיּוֹת שִׁידּוּךְ – רָאשֵׁי־תֵבוֹת: כִּי שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת וְתוֹרָה
new_packages.relationship_to_existing_package_1: Package 1 (תורה/כלה) and this proposed Package 2 (דעת/שידוך) are connected by eitza, not bechina: da'at-in-actuality flowing from the tzaddik's Torah-speech produces the shidduch between the two opposites. Torah-as-bride is the object/domain of the shidduch; da'at is the agent/force that performs it. They are two different natures — active vs. receptive — and belong in separate packages.

observations: Torah #89 is a very short Torah (5 paragraphs) with minimal bechina edges in the dataset (only one recorded). However, the text itself is rich with explicit bechina language that has not been captured. The existing single package (תורה/כלה) is genuine and correctly identified, but it covers only the secondary bechina of the Torah's argument. The primary conceptual cluster — da'at as matchmaker, the tzaddik as bar da'at, da'at in potential vs. actuality, and shidduch as the expression of da'at — forms a fully independent domain with 3+ nodes connected by explicit bechina language. This warrants a new package. The Torah's eitza structure is: da'at [pkg 2] mediates shidduchim → but da'at gets stuck when potential → hearing Torah from the tzaddik [eitza link] → da'at moves to actuality → shidduch is accomplished → Torah-as-kallah [pkg 1] is united with its groom. The good/evil mirror is notably absent in this Torah: there is no explicit evil counterpart presented. The Torah focuses entirely on the positive teaching of how shidduchim are made through da'at and Torah.
